reviews.review:
I almost quit playing this game in the first two hours of playing. The first few battles in a run are sloooooooowwwwww. You've only got three crew and only one cannon that actually does damage. It WILL take you a minimum of 6 rounds, or 18 turns, to finish a battle with the un-upgraded starter ship, just plinking away at the enemy's health with your piddly two-damage cannon shots. Boarding can be slightly faster, but only slightly. It. Is. Painful.

HOWEVER. Once you get enough gold to buy another cannon or two or enough crew and weapons to speed up boarding, this game becomes an insanely fun mashup of FTL, a roguelike deckbuilder, and XCOM. Everything is done so well. Crew classes are simple but effective. The deckbuilding part of the game is quite forgiving, with the ability to cycle your entire hand of cards for the cost of one crewmate's action. Not even their whole turn, just their action. Different cannon types and the ammo that come with them force you to strategize about how to place them on your ship and what ratios of ammo you want in your deck. The gameplay is well-balanced, although you are somewhat punished for not specializing into either cannons or boarding. 

I think my only major criticism, aside from the pacing of the first few battles, is the somewhat shallow pool of crew weapons and cannon ammunition. Currently I believe there are four ranged crew weapons, four melee crew weapons, and five cannon ammunition types. The deckbuilding itself also lacks the combo building that a true deckbuilder would have, although I think that's simply a result of marrying the deckbuilding mechanic with turn based squad combat. The unique cards associated with specific ships and captains definitely go a long way toward keeping individual runs and the decks themselves interesting. I would buy a DLC that added more mechanics, cards, weapons, or ammunition in a heartbeat.

Overall, this is an incredibly successful mash-up of three distinct genres that absolutely does not deserve the mixed reviews it currently has. Unfortunately, the pacing of the first few battles seems to have put off quite a few people, which is sad but understandable.
